response.text:
I can't delete rows without a quick confirmation and a few details — deleting spreadsheet rows is destructive, and I need to know exactly which file/sheet and which rows to target. Here's a safe, recommended plan and the choices you can confirm:

Recommended (safer) default — I can do this if you approve:
1. Inspect the specified sheet to identify candidate "test" rows (I will show a preview of matches first).
2. Copy those rows to a backup sheet named like Leads_ImportBackup_YYYYMMDD (preserves formulas/data context).
3. Permanently delete the backed-up rows from the original leads sheet.

Before I proceed I need you to confirm:
- The spreadsheet (name or share link) and the sheet/tab name.
- How to identify "test" rows. Pick one of:
  a) Any row where any cell contains the substring "test" (case-insensitive).  
  b) Any row with emails from domains like example.com, example.org, or clearly fake domains.  
  c) Any row with placeholder phone numbers (e.g., 000-000-0000) or obvious import markers.  
  d) Let me show a preview of the first 200 rows and I’ll highlight likely test rows for you to confirm.
- Whether you want the backup created (recommended) — yes/no.
- Whether to delete permanently after backup or just hide/mark them.

If you prefer I can instead just mark suspect rows with a "DELETE_CANDIDATE" tag or move them to a "Junk" sheet (non-destructive).

Tell me:
- Which spreadsheet and sheet tab to work on,
- Which identification option you want (a/b/c/d or custom),
- Whether to create a backup and whether to permanently delete.

I will wait for your confirmation before making any changes.
